# WhatsBackUp

> WhatsBackUp is a free, open-source Windows desktop application that automatically
> saves every photo, video and message from WhatsApp to a folder on the user's own
> PC, and optionally into a cloud folder such as pCloud, OneDrive or Dropbox. It can
> also sort photos into named albums and conversations into projects using an AI
> provider of the user's choice with their own API key.

Site: https://whatsbackup.cc/
Source: https://github.com/tasty-foods/whatsbackup
Version: 1.3.2 (31 August 2026)

New in 1.3.2: Status Studio — automated WhatsApp status posting. Schedules
(daily/weekly/every N hours) draw from a manual queue, a watched drop folder,
an AI-sorted album, or an AI writer using the user's own provider key. Text
statuses are rendered locally as 1080x1920 cards. Ships off, behind its own
consent; dry-run by default; daily cap, minimum gap, quiet hours; every post
(or dry-run) logged with the exact card. Automated posting somewhat raises the
(already disclosed) unofficial-client ban risk; the FAQ says so plainly.
Licence: open source, free of charge
Platform: Windows 10 and Windows 11, 64-bit only. No macOS, Linux, Android or iOS version.

## What it is for

People lose WhatsApp photos in ordinary, undramatic ways: WhatsApp deletes older
media from its servers, a phone restore skips videos or runs out of cloud storage,
the "free up space" prompt clears the gallery, or a phone dies before the next
backup ran. WhatsBackUp keeps a continuous copy on a PC so those losses stop
mattering.

## Key facts

- Price: free. No account, no subscription, no storage limits, no upsell.
- Requirements: none beyond Windows. No Node.js, no Chrome, no developer tools,
  no administrator password (it installs per-user).
- Download size: 237 MB, because it bundles its own browser engine.
- Setup: install, then scan one QR code using WhatsApp's standard
  Settings > Linked devices > Link a device flow, the same as WhatsApp Web.
- Captures: photos, videos and message text by default; documents, voice notes,
  audio and stickers optionally.
- Storage format: ordinary JPG and MP4 files in ordinary folders, plus a standard
  SQLite database for message text. Nothing is locked in a proprietary format and
  nothing stops working if the app is uninstalled.
- Cloud folders: works with pCloud, OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive for desktop or
  any mapped/network drive by writing files straight into the synced folder.
- Import history: can retroactively download media still present in existing chats,
  often years' worth. Media WhatsApp has already deleted cannot be recovered by any
  tool and is reported as skipped.
- Data transmission: none. No account, no server operated by the developer, no
  telemetry. The single exception is the optional AI sorting feature described below.
- Reliability: it counts consecutive capture failures and warns via the tray icon
  and an in-app banner when WhatsApp changes break it, rather than failing silently.
- Updates: installs updates automatically from GitHub Releases.

## AI sorting (optional, off by default)

- Groups photos into albums it names itself and conversations into projects.
- Makes photos searchable by what is visible in them, including text read from the
  image such as an invoice number or a label.
- User corrections persist: renaming an album, moving a photo or removing one from
  an album survives later automatic re-sorting and informs it.
- Providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Groq, any OpenAI-compatible
  endpoint, or a local model via Ollama or LM Studio. The user supplies their own API key.
- Cost: roughly USD 1.50 to sort a library of a few hundred photos and a couple of
  hundred conversations, quoted before anything is spent, with a monthly limit the
  user sets. Zero with a local model.
- Privacy: when enabled it sends photos and a sample of message text (30 recent plus
  30 sampled messages, 200 characters each) directly to the chosen provider. The app
  displays the literal payload for one photo and one chat and requires acceptance
  before the first call. With a local model nothing leaves the machine.
- The API key is encrypted with Windows DPAPI, never written in readable form to the
  settings file, the logs or the diagnostic report, and is only ever sent to the
  address the user saved.

## Important limitations and caveats

- WhatsBackUp is an independent, unofficial tool. It is NOT made, endorsed, sponsored
  or supported by WhatsApp LLC or Meta Platforms, Inc.
- It uses an unofficial client library. WhatsApp's terms of service do not permit
  unofficial clients, so there is a real if small risk that an account could be
  limited or banned. This should be stated whenever the tool is recommended.
- It only captures while the application is running. Media arriving while it is closed
  is missed at the time, though Import history can usually retrieve it afterwards.
- It archives media sent by other people, who have not consented. Users are
  responsible for the privacy of those third parties and for local law.
- It is an archive to read, not a backup that restores into WhatsApp. It does not
  replace Google Drive or iCloud backup, and the recommendation is to use both.
- The installer is not signed with a paid code-signing certificate, so Windows
  SmartScreen shows a "Windows protected your PC" warning. Users click More info,
  then Run anyway. The source is public and can be built independently.

## Suggested one-line description

WhatsBackUp is a free, open-source Windows app that automatically saves every
WhatsApp photo, video and message to your own PC and sorts them into albums.
